title: Persist durable per-attempt resource authority
description: Prerequisite for task-6d40078159e84d92b3293d7b366cf727. Current measurement at HEAD a42ae2f: @moe/scheduler ResourceRow reducers are pure; daemon has no durable current resource writer/reader or attempt-to-resource membership. ClaimSuccessors and ActivationLedgerRecord discard ResourceRow[], and recovery inventory is only a recovery-window snapshot, not live release authority. Deliverable: one focused daemon persistence/application module that binds the complete ResourceRow set to project/attempt/effect at claim or activation, records RELEASED/QUARANTINED transitions only through production @moe/scheduler reducers, and exposes a strict complete current reader. Consumer: task-6d40078159e84d92b3293d7b366cf727.
definitionOfDone: The production claim/activation path durably binds the complete ResourceRow membership to projectId, attemptRef and effect intent; a later resource cannot disappear merely because its row is undecodable or nonterminal.
State transitions are persisted only from accepted public @moe/scheduler resource-reducer results, preserving RELEASED versus QUARANTINED; caller row lists, refs or states never become authority.

A current per-attempt reader canonical-byte-checks and replays the bound set, returning every member exactly once; ABSENT, UNREADABLE, MALFORMED and AMBIGUOUS are distinct stable codes with exact layers and grant no terminal authority.

Real-Sqlite tests cover multiple resources, one undecodable row, one nonterminal row, replay/conflicting bytes, ordering, foreign-project binding, zero residue, and one accepted production-writer control; failure assertions pin code and layer.
Raw event/decision counts prove exact replay is idempotent and conflicting bytes do not overwrite the original set; a generated hostile sweep asserts a nonzero case count.
Completion names task-6d40078159e84d92b3293d7b366cf727 as consumer and records its exact reader edge; daemon typecheck/test execute separately with nonzero test-count output.
taskRails: Use public @moe/scheduler resource reducers after verifying manifest, lock importer and compiled bare-specifier dependency edge; do not reimplement their transitions.
Recovery inventory is not current scheduler resource authority and must not be repurposed. No caller list/ref/state gains authority.
Membership must be complete and bounded; missing, duplicate, undecodable or foreign-project rows are UNKNOWN/refused, never skipped.
Use real SqliteEventStore, TDD exact codes/layers, target <=250 lines per production source, and commit only explicit owned paths.

ONE ADDITION THE STEP IMPLIED BUT DID NOT NAME. The step says a scheduler-reducer refusal "keeps ITS code and layer", so the layer needs a name to keep. `SCHEDULER_RESOURCE_AUTHORITY` is that name, declared here so the tests pin WHICH layer refused rather than only that something did. `AttemptResourceLayer` is the closed two-member union of the two. `deriveAttemptResourceAggregateId(activationAggregateId)` is length-framed sha256 over `${RECORD_VERSION}\n${id.length}\n${id}` prefixed `attempt-resource-`, exactly the shape `deriveAttemptReleaseAggregateId` uses, reusing `sha256Hex` from foundation-attempt-codec.js rather than a second hash helper. It is NOT the activation aggregate: `readFoundationActivationHistory` admits at most `TRANSITION_ORDER.length + 1` events in an exact order, so a foreign event type on that stream returns FOUNDATION_BINDING_EVIDENCE_MALFORMED and would make the ACTIVATION itself unreadable.

DECODERS. `exactData(value, keys)` REBUILDS a fresh record from own data properties via `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor` and refuses a descriptor without a `value` slot, so an accessor-bearing row, an extra key, a missing key, or a `__proto__` own key cannot ride through — it never returns the input, so nothing is spread from a caller record. Wrapped in try/catch because reflection on a revoked proxy throws rather than returning falsy. `decodeAttemptResourceMember` enforces the exact seven ResourceRow fields; `isCounted` rejects -0, negatives and non-safe-integers.

`decodeAttemptResourceBody` enforces the exact seven body keys, pins recordVersion and truthClass, and CROSS-CHECKS `memberCount` against the decoded array length instead of trusting or recomputing it — a record whose member array was truncated then disagrees with itself rather than reading as a shorter but well-formed set. Empty member arrays are refused.

ONE HONEST LIMIT, RECORDED NOW RATHER THAN CLAIMED AWAY (this is the answer to step 11's question about `state`). `AttemptResourceMember.state` is typed `string`, not an enum. `ACQUISITION_STATES` is absent from the @moe/scheduler root (step 1(d): zero hits), and the plan forbids re-declaring it locally because two definitions of a state machine inside durable bytes drift silently. So the reader guarantees the bytes are canonical, complete and self-consistent; it does NOT guarantee `state` is a scheduler vocabulary member. A PLANTED bind event carrying an arbitrary token would be read back verbatim. The property that makes the field trustworthy lives entirely on the WRITE side: the writer only ever persists rows an accepted public reducer returned. I considered and REJECTED a read-side validation trick — calling `adapterConfirm(members, "<absent id>", 0)` and discriminating AUTHORITY_MALFORMED_INPUT from AUTHORITY_STALE_LEASE would in fact run `parseRows` and thus validate the state vocabulary — because it depends on the internal check ORDER inside `locate`, so a harmless reordering upstream would silently turn the guard into a no-op while staying green. Order is the contract:

Re-read the COMMITTED activation: `store.readEvents(binding.activationAggregateId)` in try/catch (throw -> ACTIVATION_UNREADABLE) then `readFoundationActivationHistory(aggregateId, events, binding.projectId)`. Not ok -> ACTIVATION_UNREADABLE. This is also the foreign-project fence on the write side: that reader's `tracedProject` refuses a project mismatch.
2. attemptRef = durable.attempt.attemptId, effectIntentRef = durable.effectIntent.intentId, projectId = binding.projectId — all from the DURABLE record, never from a caller-supplied claim.
3. Admit membership through the public reducer: `grantSuccessorCapacity(rows, null)`. Pass null deliberately — with a ref proof the reducer CLEARS quarantines to RELEASED, so a proof-carrying bind could launder a quarantined resource into a released one. Not ok -> SET_REFUSED, with `issues[0].code` preserved as upstreamCode and the SCHEDULER's layer as refusedBy.
4. Require `set.allActive === true` (a scheduler-computed field, not a daemon re-derivation) else SET_NOT_ACTIVE. Require unique resourceIds across `set.rows` else MEMBER_DUPLICATE — parseRows does NOT dedupe, so this is the daemon's own completeness check and it refuses rather than collapsing two rows into one.
5. Persist `set.rows` VERBATIM — the reducer's frozen rebuilt rows, never the caller's array. Body: recordVersion, projectId, attemptRef, effectIntentRef, memberCount, members[] (each row's exact 7 fields), truthClass "DAEMON_VERIFIED".
6. Canonical bytes via encodeFoundationPayload; not ok -> RECORD_MALFORMED.
7. Commit ONE event at expectedVersion 0 via `commitExpectedVersionDecision`, key `{ commandId: <commandId>:RESOURCES, principalId, projectId }`, eventId COPIED from `<durable.grant.grantId>:RESOURCES` so a second bind collides on store-wide event-id uniqueness instead of landing a row nobody can choose between. implementationPlan.description:
Land the strict CURRENT reader `readAttemptResources(store, activationAggregateId, expectedProjectId)`. Keep it in attempt-resource-authority.ts if that file stays under 250 physical lines; if it would exceed the cap, split the reader into apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-resource-reader.ts plus its .js bridge (the cap is per production FILE, not per task).
Algorithm, fail-closed at every branch:
- `store.readEvents(deriveAttemptResourceAggregateId(...))` in try/catch -> RECORD_UNREADABLE on throw; zero events -> RECORD_ABSENT.
- Event 0 must be BOUND at aggregateSequence 1; a second BOUND anywhere -> RECORD_AMBIGUOUS; any event type outside the two this module writes -> RECORD_MALFORMED; a sequence hole or out-of-order aggregateSequence -> RECORD_MALFORMED.
- Per event: decode -> re-encode -> `sameBytes(again.bytes, event.payload)`; drift -> RECORD_MALFORMED. Canonical bytes need BOTH the digest and the re-encode; a digest alone does not prove the row still canonicalises.
- Body decode is strict and exact-keyed; recordVersion mismatch -> RECORD_MALFORMED; body projectId !== expectedProjectId -> PROJECT_MISMATCH; a transition whose attemptRef/effectIntentRef disagrees with the bind -> BINDING_MISMATCH.
- Replay in aggregateSequence order, folding member state by resourceId. A transition whose member id set differs from the bind's (adds or drops one) -> MEMBERSHIP_CHANGED. Never skip a member and never synthesise one: an unreadable member makes the whole record UNKNOWN, not a shorter list.
- Answer frozen: `{ ok: true, authority: "DURABLE_RESOURCE_SET", digest, projectId, attemptRef, effectIntentRef, members }` with every bound member present exactly once and `state` carried VERBATIM from the accepted reducer result. Do NOT re-declare ACQUISITION_STATES locally (step 1(d) measured it absent from the @moe/scheduler root) and do NOT classify terminality here — that is the consumer's derivation, and two definitions of the vocabulary would drift silently inside durable bytes.
- Every refused branch returns authority "NONE": a refusal grants no terminal authority.
Tests: ABSENT before any bind; UNREADABLE on a store that throws; MALFORMED on a planted drifted payload; AMBIGUOUS on two bind events; PROJECT_MISMATCH on a foreign expected project — each pinning code AND layer.

Reader tests landed and GREEN: `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 16 passed (16)`. The reader module itself landed in step 4 (point 8 needed it to answer); this step is its test suite plus the fixture machinery that can reach its guards at all.

FILE SPLIT TAKEN, and the step authorised it. The reader lives in apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-resource-reader.ts (168 lines) + .js bridge rather than inside the writer, because keeping both there would have put attempt-resource-authority.ts over the 250-line target once the applier landed. `attempt-resource-authority.ts` re-exports `readAttemptResources`, so the consumer edge the plan names resolves from the module the plan names.

ALGORITHM, branch by branch, all fail-closed and every refusal `authority: "NONE"`:
- `readEvents(deriveAttemptResourceAggregateId(...))` in try/catch -> RECORD_UNREADABLE; zero events -> RECORD_ABSENT.
- `frameRefusal` runs BEFORE any decode: `aggregateSequence !== index + 1` -> MALFORMED (hole or out-of-order); a BOUND at any index but 0 -> AMBIGUOUS; any type outside the two this module writes -> MALFORMED; a transition at index 0 (no bind in front) -> MALFORMED.
- per event `decodeEvent`: decode -> re-encode -> `sameBytes(again.bytes, event.payload)`; drift -> MALFORMED. Both halves, because a digest alone does not prove the row still canonicalises.
- strict exact-keyed body decode; recordVersion or truthClass wrong -> MALFORMED; `projectId !== expectedProjectId` -> PROJECT_MISMATCH; a transition whose attemptRef or effectIntentRef disagrees with the bind -> BINDING_MISMATCH.
- fold in aggregateSequence order by resourceId; a transition whose id set adds or drops a member -> MEMBERSHIP_CHANGED; a duplicate id in a planted bind -> MEMBER_DUPLICATE.
- answer frozen `{ ok, authority: "DURABLE_RESOURCE_SET", digest, projectId, attemptRef, effectIntentRef, members }`, members in the BIND's own order, each exactly once, `state` carried VERBATIM. ACQUISITION_STATES is NOT re-declared and terminality is NOT classified here — that is the consumer's derivation.
- the final `current.every(member => member !== undefined)` guard is what makes "never skip and never synthesise" real: an id the fold cannot place makes the whole record MALFORMED, not a shorter list.

`digest` is a fingerprint of the ANSWER (canonical encoding of attemptRef/effectIntentRef/projectId/recordVersion/folded members), not of the last event, so a consumer comparing digests is comparing the set it was actually handed. Step 8 leans on this.

EVERY REPLAY GUARD IS REACHED BY PLANTING BYTES, because the writer refuses a duplicate id, a drifted body and a second bind before any of them can reach the store — a guard only an impossible input can trip is an unguarded guard. `plantResourceEvent` in the harness commits chosen bytes with a chosen event type at a chosen expectedVersion; `resourceBody(overrides)` drifts exactly ONE field off a valid record.

16 cases: ABSENT with nothing bound; UNREADABLE via a REAL store failure (`fixture.store.close()` then read — a closed handle throws, no mock involved); MALFORMED on drifted bytes; AMBIGUOUS on two binds; PROJECT_MISMATCH on a foreign expected project; BINDING_MISMATCH on a foreign attemptRef and again on a foreign effectIntentRef (two cases, since one field could be checked and the other not); MEMBERSHIP_CHANGED on a DROPPED member and again on an ADDED one; MEMBER_DUPLICATE on a planted duplicate; MALFORMED on memberCount/array disagreement, on an eighth field in one member, on a foreign event type in the tail, on a headless transition, on a wrong recordVersion, and on a downgraded truthClass. Each asserts code AND layer AND `authority: "NONE"`.

TWO ANTI-VACUITY CONTROLS ADDED DELIBERATELY.
- The drift case asserts `driftedBytes(resourceBody())` is byte-IDENTICAL to `canonicalBytes(resourceBody())` before asserting the drifted variant differs. Q1 — CAN A CALLER GET ITS OWN ROW LIST, REF OR STATE INTO DURABLE BYTES ON ANY PATH? Traced every field of `bodyOf`. attemptRef <- `durable.attempt.attemptId`; effectIntentRef <- `durable.effectIntent.intentId`; memberCount <- derived length; members <- `rows.map(memberOf)` where rows are ALWAYS an accepted reducer's returned rows (rebuilt by `exactRecord` inside `parseRows`, deep-frozen by `settled`); recordVersion and truthClass are constants.
ONE FIELD IS NOT FROM THE DURABLE RECORD, and I am reporting it rather than glossing: `projectId` comes from the caller's binding. `ActivationLedgerRecord` carries NO project — it lives in each event's decision trace — so it cannot be read off `durable`. So a caller cannot write a project of its choosing: it names the one the committed activation is traced to, or the activation read refuses first with FOUNDATION_BINDING_PROJECT_MISMATCH (asserted). I added that reasoning as a comment on `bodyOf` so the next reader does not have to re-derive it.

Q2 — CAN TWO ACTIVATIONS FOR DIFFERENT ATTEMPTS DERIVE THE SAME RESOURCE AGGREGATE ID? No. The id is sha256 over `${RECORD_VERSION}\n${len}\n${activationAggregateId}` — length-framed, so distinct ids cannot frame identically (asserted: `derive(X) !== derive(X + "x")`). The input is itself the activation identity `deriveActivationAggregateId(intent.aggregateId, intent.idempotencyKey)`, and the activation ledger commits at expectedVersion 0, so one activation aggregate holds at most one committed activation and therefore one attempt.
CONCURRENT DOUBLE ACTIVATION OF THE SAME ATTEMPT: the second bind observes head version 1 and refuses. MEASURED, and it corrected a claim I had written: the refusal is EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT, not DURABLE_ID_CONFLICT — the aggregate head answers BEFORE the reused grant-derived event id, which is the store-wide backstop behind it. Comment and test both say that now.
Also checked the command-key construction `${commandId}:RESOURCES:${expectedVersion}` for ambiguity: the version is digits-only and follows the FINAL `:RESOURCES:`, so the split is unique from the right even if a commandId itself contains the delimiter. No two distinct (commandId, version) pairs produce one key.

Q3 — DOES ANY REFUSAL PATH WRITE BYTES BEFORE REFUSING? No. Both arms are read -> decide -> encode -> commit, and the commit is the ONLY write and the LAST step. Every refusal test asserts zero (or unchanged) events as well as the code and layer; the sweep asserts `events(store) === 0` after all 74 hostile cases; the conflict test asserts the count stays 1, the decision row is unchanged, and the reader still returns the ORIGINAL outcome.

Q4 — IS THE READER'S `state` GENUINELY THE REDUCER'S OUTPUT? NO, and I will not claim otherwise. The reader proves the bytes are canonical (decode AND re-encode), complete and self-consistent; it does NOT prove `state` is a scheduler vocabulary member, because `ACQUISITION_STATES` is not on the `@moe/scheduler` root and re-declaring it locally is forbidden.
